content:
Jordan Lee: Dropping ADR draft here for review: enforcement point for Optimize guardrails gating (control plane + policy engine). Main open items I want feedback on: override path + audit semantics + failure modes. https://confluence.redwood/adr/adr-optimize-gating-enforcement-point (WIP)
Ethan Park: Thanks. First pass: agree control-plane enforcement, but the ADR needs to be sharper on “who blocks what” when runner/policy dependencies are down. We can’t end up with console showing blocked but API apply still proceeding via an older path.
Aditya Rao: +1. Also want clarity on the override user experience — right now it reads like “enterprise can override” but doesn’t specify approval semantics. Support/CS will ask day 1.
Naomi Feldman: From security POV: override must be least-privilege and fully auditable. We should assume overrides are exceptional and subject to review. ADR should explicitly call out RBAC + justification capture + retention.
Benji Okafor: Question on audit: are we logging the full metric breakdown per prompt? Or only aggregated metrics? We have payload size limits in audit logs.
Jordan Lee: Proposal in ADR: audit log stores (a) policy version + prompt-set revision + suite IDs, (b) aggregate metric values + pass/fail + top N failure reasons, (c) eval_run_id pointing to artifacts store. Not per-prompt in audit event.
Logan Wright: Please call out cardinality risk if we start attaching too much detail to telemetry labels. The audit event can store more, but metrics labels need to stay bounded. We should keep per-metric/per-suite only, not per prompt-set item.
Selene Huang: On failures: I’d like the ADR to define the “timeout” outcome. Applied ML is okay with “no decision = block” for most tiers, but we probably need a manual-approval path for high-touch enterprise.
Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: I’m nervous about “block on runner down” globally. If eval runner has an outage, we’ll effectively create an outage for Optimize applies. That might be acceptable if it’s staged (observe-only -> soft -> hard) and with clear paging + rollback.
Rafael Mendes: +1. ADR should include safe-degrade matrix by tenant tier + enforcement stage. Eg observe-only: allow apply but log; soft-block: allow with override; hard-block: block unless approved override (or block always).
Marcus Lin: Another security concern: override “manual approval” is still a policy decision. Who is the approver? If it’s the same user, that’s not meaningful. At minimum: separate capability, ideally second-party approval for certain tiers.
Aditya Rao: Second approver may be too heavy for GA. Could do: enterprise override requires role = “org admin + support escalation” and captures justification + creates an internal review ticket. But we need to decide now.
Chloe Martin: From console side: we can support these states, but if approval is async, that’s a bigger UX lift. If the ADR says “second approver” we need workflow work (requests queue, status, notifications).
Jordan Lee: Right, trying to keep the ADR focused on architecture, not full workflow. But we need to specify minimum requirements so implementation isn’t ambiguous.
Naomi Feldman: Minimum requirements I’d insist on:
- Override action gated by RBAC (separate permission)
- Mandatory justification string (min length)
- Audit event includes requester + actor + justification + policy/eval versions + final decision
- Rate limiting to prevent “override as default”
- Ability to export audit events (SIEM)
Marcus Lin: +1, plus we should avoid logging prompt content in audit artifacts by default. Prompt sets can contain customer data.
Selene Huang: Re: prompt content, eval harness already supports redaction modes, but ADR should say: artifacts stored encrypted, retention limited, access restricted.
Logan Wright: If artifacts are in object storage, we need consistent IDs across hosted/dedicated/private so correlation works. Also: retention policy needs to be explicit (eg 30d artifacts, 1y summaries, 7y audit minimal fields) — otherwise we’ll have customers asking.
Ethan Park: Also worried about determinism: policy engine should be the single decision-maker. Console shouldn’t “compute pass/fail” from metrics; it should display decision + reasons. ADR should mention this to avoid drift.
Jordan Lee: That’s in the “decision ownership” section but I can strengthen it. The API returns `decision=PASS|FAIL|TIMEOUT|ERROR` and `reasons[]` computed server-side.
Benji Okafor: Another edge: concurrency. If two Optimize applies happen simultaneously on same route/model, we can race (one passes, one fails, or one overwrites config). ADR should say enforcement ties to config version / optimistic locking.
Ethan Park: Yes — the “apply” must include prior config hash or version, otherwise we can’t guarantee the eval ran against the right baseline.
Jonas Weber: From eval methodology: also need to pin model version + prompt-set rev + grader versions. Otherwise you’ll see “flaky gating decisions” and we’ll never debug it.
Sean Gallagher: Failure modes section should include:
- runner backlog / timeouts
- eval harness returns partial results
- policy schema mismatch / unknown metric
- artifacts store down
For each: what does apply do, what do we alert on, and how do we recover.
Rafael Mendes: Also: what’s the max latency we tolerate in apply flow? If we make apply synchronous waiting for evals, the console will feel broken. I assume async job + polling.
Chloe Martin: Current UX spec assumes async with a “pending” state and then pass/fail. But we need a hard cap where it becomes TIMEOUT and the user can “rerun” or “request override”.
Aditya Rao: Product preference: default cap 20 min for full suite; if it’s longer it’s probably stuck/backlogged. But we should have per-suite SLAs.
Jordan Lee: ADR currently assumes async runner. I’ll update with an explicit “apply call triggers eval job, returns gating_run_id, UI polls / webhook optional” and the enforcement occurs at the moment of actual config write.
Ethan Park: Important: don’t allow “apply config now, revert if fail later”. It must gate before write, otherwise rollback is not enough (customer sees regression).
Aditya Rao: Yep, hard requirement.
Marcus Lin: On audit logging: ADR should specify immutable log semantics. Append-only event stream (even if exported). If we allow edits/deletes, we’ll fail customer audits.
Naomi Feldman: +1. Also include “override used” boolean + “override reason code” for reporting.
Logan Wright: For telemetry: recommend emitting both (a) audit event (append-only), and (b) metrics counters for pass/fail/timeout by tier + optimization type. But do NOT include tenant_id in metrics labels. Use internal dimension mapping in logs if needed.
Benji Okafor: Where do we store threshold policy versions? ADR says “versioned config service” but doesn’t say migration. If policy schema changes, how do old policies behave?
Jordan Lee: That’s the other ADR (threshold schema + versioning). But I can link it and add a line: policy evaluation supports pinned versions; schema changes are additive; old versions remain evaluable.
Jonas Weber: Please add note: metric names are stable identifiers, not display strings. We’ve had issues with “rubric_score” vs “rubric.overall” drifting.
Selene Huang: +1, and we need a place to record “known bad transitions” for quantization. Even if policy engine holds it, the ADR should mention enforcement supports per-model exclusions.
Sean Gallagher: Finally: who owns the oncall for the gating service + policy eval path? If control plane is enforcement, SRE will page Control Plane team, not Applied ML. ADR should set ownership boundaries.
Jordan Lee: Ack. I’ll add ownership section: Control Plane owns enforcement + availability; Applied ML owns threshold values + suite content; SRE owns alerting + rollout guardrails.
Connor O'Brien: Release/process note: if we’re going to hard-block, we need a flag stage plan in the ADR (observe-only -> soft-block -> hard-block) and explicit rollback lever.
Aditya Rao: +1, otherwise Product will get pulled into incident decisions.
Jordan Lee: Got it. Action items from this thread:
- strengthen failure-mode matrix + safe-degrade by tier/stage
- specify determinism (policy engine decides; UI displays)
- add override minimum requirements (RBAC, justification, audit fields, rate limits)
- add optimistic locking / config version pinning
- clarify audit vs artifacts content + retention
- add ownership + rollout stages
I’ll update draft tonight and re-request review.
Ethan Park: :thumbsup: please tag me on the updated section about config versioning/locking.
Naomi Feldman: Tag me on override + audit semantics.
Sean Gallagher: Tag me on failure modes + safe-degrade.
Jonas Weber: Tag me on pinning model/prompt-set/grader versions.
Jordan Lee: Will do.
